technical_and_design_decisions: Implement module contributions through the existing Spring Cloud Data Flow server/module-registry abstractions rather than introducing a separate registry service.
Persist dynamically contributed module metadata so registrations survive server restart and become immediately available to stream and task definition operations.
Expose module registration through REST and provide corresponding shell commands that invoke the REST/API service consistently.
Validate required module coordinates, type, name, version, and URI fields at registration time and reject duplicate or malformed registrations with clear errors.
Migrate the JMS, Mail, Mongo, MQTT, Reactor IP, and Stdout modules as independently buildable Spring Cloud Stream source modules using the repository's existing conventions.

Reuse existing Spring XD module behavior where compatible, while adapting configuration properties, metadata, dependencies, packaging, and tests to the target Spring Cloud Stream/Data Flow repositories.
Use automated unit and integration tests for registry persistence, REST behavior, shell behavior, duplicate handling, and each migrated module's primary processing path.
Update build configuration, module metadata, documentation, and CI configuration so the new modules and registry functionality are reproducible and discoverable.
assumptions: The increment targets an existing Spring Cloud Data Flow-era codebase with established REST, shell, module registry, build, and test infrastructure.
Existing module registry persistence mechanisms can be extended without introducing a new database technology or migration framework.
The specification does not require a new authentication or authorization model; existing application security is retained.
The existing Spring XD implementations and their licenses, dependencies, and behavior are available for migration.
Each migrated module has one primary source behavior and does not require major feature expansion beyond making it usable in a streaming pipeline.
Compatibility with the repository's existing Java, Spring Cloud Stream, messaging binder, and packaging versions is assumed; resolving ordinary dependency incompatibilities is included.

The work is estimated for one developer and includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation, and release/build verification, but not production operations or long-term maintenance.
No major redesign of the shell or REST API conventions is required, and existing API versioning and error-handling patterns can be followed.
Work-hour estimates are most-likely estimates and exclude elapsed waiting time for external approvals or unavailable environments.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the current module registry bootstrap flow, persistence model, REST endpoints, shell commands, module conventions, Spring XD source modules, and existing test/build infrastructure; identify compatibility and migration impacts.

Define the dynamic registration data model, persistence lifecycle, validation rules, REST resource and error contracts, shell command behavior, duplicate semantics, and migration structure for the six modules.

Replace or extend hard-coded bootstrap registration with persistent runtime registration, implement registry service and repository changes, support lookup by module type/name/version, and ensure newly registered modules are immediately available to definition creation.

activities.activity_name: REST API for custom module upload and registration
activities.activity_description: Implement REST endpoints for contributing module metadata/artifact information, request validation, duplicate handling, response models, error responses, and integration with the dynamic registry service.
Add shell command(s) for registering or uploading custom modules, including command parsing, required options, REST client integration, output formatting, and user-facing error handling.

activities.activity_name: Registry API and persistence integration testing
activities.activity_description: Verify registration, restart persistence, immediate discoverability, duplicate and invalid input behavior, REST responses, shell interaction, and compatibility with stream/task definition creation.
Port the JMS module into the target Spring Cloud Stream module repository, adapt configuration and dependencies, add module metadata and packaging, and implement module-specific tests.
Port the Mail module, adapt Spring configuration and dependency versions, provide target repository metadata and packaging, and verify its source behavior with automated tests.
Port the Mongo module, adapt Mongo and messaging integration configuration, add target-compatible metadata and packaging, and test document/event emission behavior.
Port the MQTT module, adapt MQTT client and binder configuration, add module metadata and packaging, and test message consumption and emission into a stream pipeline.
Port the Reactor IP module, adapt reactive networking and stream integration code, add metadata and packaging, and test its primary reactive source behavior.
Port the Stdout module, adapt its source/output configuration and packaging, add module metadata, and verify output behavior with focused tests.
Run the complete build and test suite, verify module discovery and registration for all migrated modules, exercise representative stream definitions, and fix integration or compatibility defects.
Document REST and shell registration workflows, request fields, validation/errors, persistence behavior, migrated module names and properties, and representative streaming pipeline examples.

activities.activity_name: Build, CI, packaging, and release verification
activities.activity_description: Update build descriptors and CI jobs, verify dependency and artifact publication configuration, perform clean-build and packaging checks, and prepare the increment for delivery.

activities.activity_name: Final defect correction and delivery preparation
activities.activity_description: Address defects found during final validation, clean up implementation, confirm acceptance criteria, and assemble the final change set and release notes.
